title: Restricted injective module sheaves are acyclic for étale direct image
statement: Let Λ and Λ′ be commutative rings in Type(u+1), φ:Λ→Λ′ a ring homomorphism, and f:Z→W a morphism of schemes. For an injective sheaf I of Λ′-modules on Z_et, the Λ-module sheaf Res_φ I is f_*-acyclic: for every n≥0 the object (R^(n+1) f_*)(Res_φ I) is zero. Direct image is that of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and acyclicity is [def-sp-acyclic]. Neither flatness of φ nor quasi-compactness of f is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03FD, proof, via Čech vanishing on every object and every slice; Tag 0D6J(3) for coefficient-independent direct image.

proof.text: Apply the invertibility of the canonical module/abelian derived direct-image comparison for both Λ and Λ′. The definition of rightDerivedBaseChange evaluates its image under the homology functor, so the classical degree-(n+1) comparison is invertible as well.

Positive classical derived direct image of the injective Λ′-module sheaf I is zero by Functor.isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ. Forgetting coefficients preserves zero objects; transport through the Λ′ comparison to obtain vanishing of abelian higher direct image of I_ab.

The underlying abelian sheaf of Res_φ I equals I_ab definitionally. Transport the preceding vanishing through the Λ comparison. The forgetful sheaf functor is faithful and preserves zero morphisms: its image of the identity is zero, so the identity of the Λ-module higher direct image is zero. By IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero that object is zero. This holds in every positive degree and is precisely rightAcyclic.

proof_origin.note: Use the existing canonical derived coefficient comparison for both rings, then reflect zero objects through the faithful coefficient-forgetting functor.
